title: Rust: Scope and Ownership
description: Understand variable scope, ownership, and borrowing in Rust.

steps.title: Block Scope
steps.description: Declare `x = 10` outside a block. Inside a block `{}`, declare `y = 20`. Print both x and y inside and outside.
hints: Variables declared inside `{}` are scoped to that block.
`x` is accessible both inside and outside.
`y` is only accessible inside the block.

verification.failureMessage: Print x outside and y inside the block.

steps.title: Ownership Transfer (Move)
steps.description: Declare `let s1 = String::from("hello");`, then `let s2 = s1;`. Try to print `s1` (it will fail — comment it out). Print `s2`.
hints: `String` does not implement `Copy`, so assignment moves ownership.
After `let s2 = s1;`, `s1` is no longer valid.

verification.failureMessage: Print s2 after moving from s1.

steps.title: Clone (Deep Copy)
steps.description: Declare `let s1 = String::from("hello");`, then `let s2 = s1.clone();`. Now both are valid — print both.
hints: .clone() creates a deep copy of the heap data.
After cloning, both variables are valid.
This is more expensive than a move but allows independent values.

verification.successMessage: Clone works! Both strings are independent.
verification.failureMessage: Print both s1 and s2 after cloning.

steps.title: Borrowing with References
steps.description: Create a String `s = String::from("borrow")`. Write a function `print_str(s: &String)` that prints it. Call with `&s`. After the call, s is still usable in main.
hints: The function signature `fn print_str(s: &String)` borrows s.
After calling `print_str(&s)`, you can still use `s` in main.

verification.failureMessage: Print the string via a borrowed reference.

steps.title: Copy Types
steps.description: Show that primitive types like `i32` implement `Copy`. Declare `let a = 5; let b = a;` then print both `a` and `b`.
hints: After `let b = a;`, both `a` and `b` are still valid.
This is because `i32` is stored on the stack (cheap to copy).

verification.successMessage: Copy types work! Both variables are valid.
verification.failureMessage: Print both a and b to show Copy behavior.
